Cancels the vanilla zombie AI pathing a bandit to a player it cannot see. Paths towards a noise are left alone.
Writes what the fixes are doing to the console. Only useful when reporting a problem.
How far from the exact tile still counts as holding the post. 15 means one and a half tiles.
How close you have to be before a bandit notices you without seeing you. Also caps the Recon and Tracker bonuses.
Puts the clothing a bandit was wearing onto its body. Turn this off if another mod already does it.

Marks every bandit close enough to be loaded on the world map and the minimap: red for hostiles, blue for your companions. It cannot show the whole county - only what your game is already loading around you, so a group still warns you before you can see where it came from. Turn it off if you would rather not know.
Draws friendly NPCs on the map as well, in blue. Applies to both of the other map options.
Also place them as map symbols (for second-screen map mods)

Second-screen map mods such as PZ Map redraw the map themselves and cannot see the overlay above, so this registers the bandits as real map symbols instead, which they do read. Warning: map symbols are your saved annotations. They are removed again every second and when you switch this off, but if the game is killed outright a few stamps can be left on your map for you to delete by hand. Off by default for that reason.
Hide the warning once they are dead
How close you must be to the marked spot before an empty area counts as 'all dead' rather than 'not loaded yet'.
Removes the warning as soon as no bandit of that side is left alive nearby.
Points the arrow at where the closest living bandit is right now, instead of the tile the group spawned on.
Several groups arriving in a row stack arrows on top of each other. Keeps only the newest one per side.
After losing sight of you, bandits search where they last saw you for this long. Set to 0 to make them forget instantly.
Also show them on the minimap

The minimap is on screen the whole time, so bandit dots there mean you always roughly know where they are. Turn this off to keep them on the world map only, which you have to open on purpose. Has no effect unless the option above is on.
What friendly NPCs are allowed to break. Hostile bandits are never restricted.
Lets a companion hold a post it is standing next to, instead of looping between the post and you.
Bandits notice you only by sight or sound
Limits the AI's player sensor to line of sight, hearing at close range, or being attacked - the same rules zombies play by.
Free NPCs running on the spot
How long an NPC has to fail to move before the watchdog resets it.
Drops the path and picks a new goal when an NPC on a move order stops covering ground. Never teleports.
